## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f2642c6b00517340a4b23cb1b8e4f1d157b9e8f0`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.package-less-row-exact-address-by-type-class.ts` + `.changeset/32568-package-less-row-sealed-and-draft-exits.md`, `.changeset/32968-package-less-row-remedy-order.md` (read only where they restate the entry)

Inputs: card #32968 (body and its one comment), card #32568 and the entry it registered, PR #32973 body, file list and net diff at the head, the head's check-runs at review time. Code on `main` (`25ee50765`, the PR's merge base) was read, not reviewed: `protocol-diff-delete-load.ts` (delete door), `protocol-environment-rows.ts` and `protocol-lock-version-gates.ts` (`packagelessAddress`, `packagelessDraftAddress`), `protocol-write-gates.ts` (`refusePackagedBaseRemoval`, `isSealedManagedItem`, `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal`), `sys-metadata-repository.ts` (`delete`, `unboundItemDraftAddress`), `metadata-plugin.zod.ts` (type flags), `override-declaration.zod.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

The entry changes what an upgrader is told to do: `replacement` now leads with "delete the package-less row FIRST" through `DELETE /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME` naming no package, splits remedy (1) by holder kind (writable holder at `?package=ID`; code package in `?package=ID.custom` with `overrides: { package: ID, basedOn: VERSION }`), and reorders (2a). `acceptanceCriteria` name the address the saved draft answers at. `id`, `surface` and `reason` are unchanged; no key, export or answer moves.

The diagnosis the PR rests on is confirmed by the code on `main`:

- The delete door resolves a delete naming no package to `request.packageId ?? (draftAddress.key | rowsAtAddress.packageId)`. `packagelessAddress` returns the one package the rows at that state are bound to, so with one bound row beside the package-less row the bound row is the one removed. For drafts, `packagelessDraftAddress` returns the holder's own draft when the item's active rows are bound to that holder and it has a draft. Save-then-delete therefore removes the saved row in the writable-holder draft case and the (2a) `dataset` override case, as the PR says.
- `namedBaseOverlayWriteRefusal` closes a save naming a read-only code package and names its pair; the `overrides` shape in the entry matches `override-declaration.zod.ts`.
- Delete-first is the right order for the cases the PR measured (`email_template`, `dashboard`, `dataset`).

The direction is right. The text as written is not yet a remedy an operator can follow to the intended state for every type it covers, and its first step is destructive without a stated precondition (see ④).

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` at `patch`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, stated on the PR body and in the new changeset, and unchanged in the edited one. Correct for a text-only correction of an already registered ADR-0087 entry: the entry's `id` is unchanged, nothing is added to the published surface, and no reader's answer moves. The level-axis step of `Check Changeset` agrees in its log ("a non-protocol change at patch"). No finding on the level.

### ③ Boundary flags

- should-fix: `Check Changeset` is `failure` on this head. The failing step refuses the edit of `.changeset/32568-package-less-row-sealed-and-draft-exits.md`, a pending note that exists on the merge base and was not added by this PR (#17712). The edit is a deliberate correction, and the gate's stated remedy is to declare the DELIBERATE CORRECTION on the PR, naming the note; the PR body carries no such declaration. Do not restore the note from base.
- The card's file surface also names `.changeset/32568-package-less-row-upgrade-guide-entry.md`. It is untouched, and correctly: it carries no remedy sentence.
- Diff is the three files named; no product code. The branch-history note in the PR body (#32820's commits reverted to `main`'s text) does not show in the net diff.
- At review time most other check-runs on the head (Build Core, Test Core shards, Type Check, Lint, Test UI) were still in progress; none had failed besides the one above.

### ④ Design judgment

Walked step by step against the code on `main`.

**must-fix 1. The delete is prescribed first and nothing tells the operator to capture the row's body before it.** `SysMetadataRepository.delete` hard-deletes the `sys_metadata` row. For `state: 'draft'` it writes no history row at all; for an active row it writes a history row with `metadata: null`. So for remedy (1), whose subject is a draft, step one erases the only stored copy of the customization, and "then save the change where it belongs" has nothing to save from unless the operator already holds the body. The old order kept the row until the save had succeeded; the new order removes that net, and a save that is then refused (the pair cannot be ensured, the override write gate refuses the declared body, a `basedOn` that does not match) leaves nothing to retry from. A sealed type's package-less row is, in the entry's own words, served by no read, so its body is not on screen either. The remedy must start with reading and keeping the package-less row's body (and say where it can be read), in `replacement`, and the edited changeset must say the same. As written, an operator following the corrected remedy literally loses the customization the card exists to protect.

**must-fix 2. The one delete door the entry now names refuses for most of class (2).** `deleteMetaItemUnaudited` calls `refusePackagedBaseRemoval` before any row is probed, on an environment kernel, whenever the request names no pair. It throws `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` ("sealed against removal") when the name is artifact-backed and the type has neither `allowEnvironmentOverlay` nor `supportsOverlay`. By the type flags in `metadata-plugin.zod.ts` that is `flow`, `action`, `doc`, `mapping` of (2a) and `hook`, `job`, `queue`, `sharing_rule`, `assignment_rule`, `agent`, `api` of (2b); only `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `book` and `skill` pass the removal carve-out. `main` records the same fact in `packages/objectql/src/protocol-registry-heal-packageless-refusal.test.ts` ("the package-less row of a name code packages ship is sealed against removal, 403", for `action`). So "Delete the package-less row FIRST (DELETE /api/v1/meta/TYPE/NAME naming no package)" cannot be executed for eleven of the types the entry lists, and the acceptance criterion "no package-less row of the name remains" cannot be met through it. The PR measured `email_template`, `dashboard` and `dataset` only, none of which is in the refused set. The old text was vague about the door; the new text names one and generalises it to every case. Either name the door that removes such a row for these types, or state per type what the operator does when the delete answers 403 (for the (2a) members among them the declared override can still be saved, and no order loses it, because the package-less delete never reaches a row). No data is lost on this path; the remedy simply stops at step one.

**should-fix 3. Delete-first is safe only when no row at that state is already bound to a package.** The entry states the mechanism ("a package-less delete addresses the one package the name's rows are bound to") but applies it only to the row "just saved". The same resolution bites a row that was there before the upgrade: an existing declared override in `ID.custom` beside the package-less active row, or the holder's own pending draft beside the package-less draft when the active rows are bound to that holder. There the first delete removes the bound row and leaves the package-less one; with two bound packages it answers `409`. `request.packageId ?? ...` treats `null` as absent, so the door has no way to name the package-less row. The entry should tell the operator to check that the name has no package-bound row at that state (or to read the delete's receipt, which names `(package=ID)` and what remains) and what to do when one exists.

**nit 4.** The (2a) sentence now reads "author the change ... after deleting the package-less row", which is consistent with the lead; it inherits must-fix 2 for `flow`, `action`, `doc` and `mapping`. The acceptance-criteria clause that a code package's own `?package=ID&state=draft` "answers no draft" rests on the PR's measurement; it was not confirmed by read here.

The (1) split by holder kind and the corrected (2a) order hold against the code for the overlay types and for `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `book`. The two changesets agree with the entry and so carry the same two defects.

The door it names exists: `sys_metadata` declares `apiEnabled: true` with `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`, and the stored body is the row's `metadata` column for a draft as for an active row (`draft_changes` is a separate provenance column). The parenthesis "a delete naming ID or ID.custom removes nothing either" holds: naming the base hits the same 403, and naming the pair is admitted as a pair-row removal and finds no row there before the override is saved. The acceptance criteria carry the matching exception, so they are satisfiable.

### ④ Design judgment

Walked again against `main`, per type class.

- (1) overlay drafts, code holders: package-less draft with no active row bound, or one bound: `packagelessDraftAddress` resolves to the unbound draft unless the bound package has its own draft, which the new precondition tells the operator to clear first. Delete then removes the package-less draft; the save lands in `ID.custom`. Holds.
- (1) writable holder: active rows bound to the holder, the holder has no draft: the delete removes the unbound draft; the save at `?package=ID` follows. Holds.
- (2) `page`, `app`, `dataset`, `book`: the delete passes the removal carve-out and `assertDeleteAllowed` (overlay-capable), and `packagelessOverlayWriteRefusal` does not apply to these types. An existing override in `ID.custom` is removable at its own address (pair-row removal); after it, the package-less delete reaches the unbound row. Then the declared override is saved. Ends with no package-less row. Holds.
- (2b) `skill`: same delete path as above; the change ships in the package's source or under its own name. Holds.
- (2a) `flow`, `action`, `doc`, `mapping` and the rest of (2b): the delete is skipped; the override is saved (lane measured `action` and `flow`; `doc`, `mapping` and the (2b) types rest on the flags, which this read confirms). The row remains and the entry says so.

Findings on the new text:

**should-fix 1. The draft delete reads the name's ACTIVE bindings, and the precondition only looks "at that state".** `packagelessDraftAddress` returns `ambiguous` whenever the item's active rows are bound to two or more packages, whatever drafts exist, and the delete door then answers `409`. The operator checks draft-state rows as told, finds none bound, and the package-less draft delete still answers 409; the entry's "(409 when two)" points at rows of the same state, so it does not explain this, and the only way through the door would be removing a live active row. No data is lost (the delete is refused), but the remedy cannot be completed there and the text does not say so. Say that the draft delete is decided by the active rows' bindings and what the operator does when two packages have active rows (or state honestly that the package-less draft then stays). Read from code, not run.

**should-fix 2. "fold it into the change you save" is wrong when the cleared row belongs to another package.** With two holders, the bound row the package-less delete would hit can be the other holder's override or draft. Folding its body into the change saved under the first holder moves one holder's customization onto the other's item. The text should say to re-save that row at its own address after the package-less delete, and fold only when it is the same package the change is going to.

**nit 3.** "No metadata read serves it" is stated for every case, but for an overlay draft the strict draft read naming no package can address the unbound draft; the data-route instruction is still correct. "with package_id empty" should say null or empty. The 403 is taken on an environment kernel (the gate sits under `environmentId !== undefined`); the PR body records the host-config difference, the entry does not. None changes the end state.

The edited changeset restates the same steps and the same per-type 403 sentences, and agrees with the entry; the new changeset's summary agrees too. Both inherit the two should-fix items.
